title: Fppf descent of flat finitely presented proper-support families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_BT}$-module, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$. Here finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules; flatness is stalkwise flatness over base local rings on etale charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]; proper support means $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\times_BT$ with $Z\to T$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Modules and tensor pullback use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$; composition uses canonical pullback composition isomorphisms. These groupoids and pullback transitions form a stack in groupoids on the big fppf site of $S$: isomorphism presheaves are sheaves, and every covering descent datum for objects is effective [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

proof.text: For any $T\to B$, the projection $X_T\to T$ is locally of finite type: this is the chartwise base-change assertion explicitly included in [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor] for a finitely presented space morphism. Hence [lem-sfb-space-module-base-change-flat-proper-support] applies to every scheme map $v:T'\to T$. It shows that $(bv,v_X^*M)$ again satisfies all four module conditions, even when $v$ is not flat. Thus the displayed transitions are defined on objects and, by functoriality of tensor pullback, on isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08W5, lemma-coherent-fibred-in-groupoids, first lifting condition; Situation 08KB

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] for the canonical pullback composition comparisons. On local tensor representatives these send $a\otimes(b\otimes m)$ to $a\,v^\sharp(b)\otimes m$. For three pullbacks both parenthesizations send a triple tensor to the product of its scalar factors times $m$; the identity comparison sends $1\otimes m$ to $m$. These identities respect balancing and hence sheafification, giving the unit and associativity identities. The fibre arrows are invertible by definition. For arrows $(v_1,\phi_1):x_1\to x$ and $(v_2,\phi_2):x_2\to x$ and $h$ with $v_2h=v_1$, the unique filler $x_1\to x_2$ is $(h,\phi_1\circ h_X^*(\phi_2^{-1}))$, with the composition comparison understood. Applying $\phi_2$ proves the required factorization and also uniqueness. This verifies both lifting conditions for a category fibred in groupoids as defined in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

Fix two objects over $T$ and an fppf cover $\{U_i\to U\}$ of any $T$-scheme $U$, with compatible isomorphisms between their restrictions. Their base maps $U\to B$ agree: they agree on every $U_i$, and $B$ is an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Call the common base map $b$. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus], $\{X_U\times_U U_i\to X_U\}$ is an fppf cover. Full faithfulness in [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] descends the compatible module maps uniquely. It also descends their inverses; faithfulness gives both inverse identities since these hold on the cover. Conversely restrictions of any global isomorphism are compatible. This proves the entire isomorphism presheaf is a sheaf, including uniqueness and the case where no isomorphism exists.

source.place: Tag 08KC, lemma-coherent-stack, isomorphism sheaves; direct fully faithful descent in place of the diagonal argument

proof.text: Let $\{a_i:T_i\to T\}$ be an fppf cover and let $(b_i:T_i\to B,M_i,\varphi_{ij})$ be an object descent datum. Its overlap arrows force $b_i\operatorname{pr}_i=b_j\operatorname{pr}_j$. The fppf sheaf condition for $B$ in [def-trf-algebraic-space] gives a unique $b:T\to B$ with $ba_i=b_i$. Set $Y=X\times_B T$ and $Y_i=Y\times_T T_i=X\times_B T_i$, with projections $q_i:Y_i\to Y$. The fibre-product identities also identify $Y_i\times_Y Y_j$ with $X\times_B(T_i\times_T T_j)$, and similarly for triples. By [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus] the $q_i$ form an fppf cover. Thus the $\varphi_{ij}$ are exactly a module descent datum on that cover. Essential surjectivity in [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] gives a quasi-coherent $M$ on $Y$ and isomorphisms $q_i^*M\simeq M_i$ realizing the prescribed overlap maps. It remains to verify the three additional conditions on $M$.

source.place: Tag 08KC, lemma-coherent-stack, descent of the base map and effectivity via Tag 04W8

proof.text: For an etale scheme chart $U\to Y$, put $U_i=U\times_T T_i$. These are schemes and form an fppf cover of $U$ by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. It is an fpqc scheme cover by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. The small-etale module $M|_U$ corresponds to a quasi-coherent Zariski module $G$; [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies its ordinary pullback to $U_i$ with the tensor pullback of $M|_U$ along $U_i\to U$; the composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] for the square $U_i\to U\to Y$, $U_i\to Y_i\to Y$, together with $q_i^*M\simeq M_i$, identify this with $M_i|_{U_i}$. Each is finitely presented, since $U_i\to Y_i$ is etale; the etale and Zariski finite-presentation conditions agree by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] now gives finite presentation of $G$. The same comparison gives finite presentation of $M|_U$. Doing this for an etale atlas of $Y$ proves that $M$ is finitely presented by the chart criterion of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus].

source.place: Tag 08KC, finite-presentation verification; spaces-descent.tex Tag 060V, lemma-finite-presentation-descends, realized by scheme descent on charts

proof.text: Keep any etale scheme chart $U\to Y$ and its quasi-coherent Zariski module $G$. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and the composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], its pullback $G_i$ to $U_i=U\times_T T_i$ is the Zariski module of $M_i|_{U_i}$. For every $u\in U$, choose $i$ and $u_i\in U_i$ above $u$, using joint surjectivity from [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. The module $(G_i)_{u_i}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T_i,t_i}$ by the relative flatness of $M_i$. The scheme map $a_i$ is flat at $t_i$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change] to the cartesian square $U_i\to U$, $T_i\to T$: it gives that $G_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. This holds on every chart and at every point, exactly the relative flatness required of $M$. No flatness of $Y\to T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08KC, relative-flatness verification; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05VW, lemma-base-change-module-flat, reduced to more-morphisms.tex Tag 047C

proof.text: Finite presentation implies finite type by the local finite presentation, so [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] defines $Z=V(\operatorname{Ann}M)\hookrightarrow Y$. We verify that $Z\times_T T_i$ is the scheme-theoretic support $Z_i$ of $M_i$. On any affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ let $N=M(U)$, a finite $A$-module by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. Cover $U_i=U\times_T T_i$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$. The scheme map $U_i\to U$ is flat by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus], so $A\to C$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. The chart tensor comparison [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], the Zariski-etale comparison [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] identify $M_i(V)$ with $N\otimes_A C$. Since $M|_U$ is the module associated with $N$, a function on $U$ kills every local section of $M$ iff it kills $N$, so $\operatorname{Ann}(M)(U)=\operatorname{Ann}_A(N)$; likewise $\operatorname{Ann}(M_i)(V)=\operatorname{Ann}_C(M_i(V))$. Hence [lem-trf-annihilator-finite-flat-base-change] gives $\operatorname{Ann}_C(M_i(V))=\operatorname{Ann}_A(N)C$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence] the ideal of the pulled-back closed subspace is the image of $q_i^*\operatorname{Ann}(M)\to\mathcal O_{Y_i}$, whose sections on $V$ are, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] and the image clause of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus], the image of $\operatorname{Ann}_A(N)\otimes_AC\to C$, namely $\operatorname{Ann}_A(N)C$. Equality on these covering charts gives $Z_i=Z\times_T T_i$ as closed subspaces, rather than only equality of underlying supports.

source.place: Tag 08KC, scheme-theoretic support; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 089C, lemma-flat-pullback-support, from algebra.tex Tag 07T8 on affine charts

proof.text: Each $M_i$ has a proper closed carrier by hypothesis. Applying [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] to $Y_i\to T_i$ shows that $Z_i\to T_i$ is proper. Its local-finite-type hypothesis holds for $Y_i=X\times_B T_i\to T_i$ by the assertion in [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]; the same holds for $Y\to T$. Step 7 identifies $Z_i$ with $Z\times_T T_i$. Properness in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] therefore gives that $Z\to T$ is proper. The converse implication of [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] supplies a finite type module on this proper closed carrier whose pushforward is $M$. Thus $(b,M)$ is an object of $\mathcal C(T)$ and the isomorphisms from step 4 realize the original object descent datum. Together with steps 2 and 3 this proves the fppf stack assertion.
